company.name: Northstar Retail Group
company.summary: Omnichannel retailer with stores, ecommerce, loyalty, merchandising, and supply-chain operations.

strategic_priorities: Reduce legacy ADM run-cost and rebalance spend toward innovation
Create a real-time inventory and fulfillment decision layer
Improve digital conversion, loyalty personalization, and release velocity
Industrialize support with AI-assisted operations and observability
pain_points: Fragmented application estate across stores, ecommerce, merchandising, and supply chain
High dependency on aging POS, order, and merchandising platforms
Slow release cycles and duplicated data pipelines
Inconsistent customer identity, offer, and returns experiences across channels
operating_model_notes: Stores and digital channels share inventory and fulfillment responsibilities
The client wants margin improvement without slowing innovation

current_state_metrics.name: Customer-facing release cadence
current_state_metrics.evidence_note: Modeled from current-state release governance review and platform dependency mapping.

current_state_metrics.name: P1 incident MTTR
current_state_metrics.evidence_note: Modeled from current-state support operations review and major incident patterns.

current_state_metrics.name: Inventory sync latency
current_state_metrics.evidence_note: Modeled from batch interface timing across inventory, order, and fulfillment workflows.

current_state_metrics.name: Duplicate customer record rate
current_state_metrics.evidence_note: Modeled from identity-resolution issues across loyalty, ecommerce, and service systems.

execution_assumptions: Holiday code freeze applies from mid-November through early January for customer-facing platforms.
Target delivery-mix shift to 55% offshore is achieved by year 3, with architecture and product ownership remaining onshore-led.
Architecture review board meets monthly and transformation design authority meets weekly during active modernization waves.
Wave 1 prioritizes customer identity, pricing, returns, and observability foundations before major order and supply-chain rewrites.
Platform engineering capacity is shared across commerce, loyalty, and supply-chain programs, so sequencing must avoid parallel peak demand.

assumption_provenance.assumption_basis: Modeled transformation investment envelope for a five-year modernization partnership.
Target-state product, architecture, and governance roles remain onshore-led.
North America timezone coverage is reserved for business analysis and product operations roles.
Year-3 target state assumes engineering factory and shared platform services scale offshore.
Modeled engineering and support productivity uplift from AI-assisted delivery and automation.
Assumes slightly above half of gross productivity is monetized as capacity creation or cost takeout.
Modeled avoidance value tied to incident reduction, outage prevention, and control automation.
Full run-cost retirement is assumed once legacy platform decommission completes.
Retained apps assume marginal efficiency only from support standardization.
Lift-and-shift actions assume infrastructure savings without major functional redesign.
Platform modernization assumes moderate operations and infrastructure efficiency gains.
Code and platform refactoring assume higher supportability and automation benefits.
Strategic rearchitecture assumes the largest long-run operating model simplification.

business_problem: Fragmented application estate across stores, ecommerce, merchandising, and supply chain
High dependency on aging POS, order, and merchandising platforms
Slow release cycles and duplicated data pipelines
Inconsistent customer identity, offer, and returns experiences across channels
